claim_text: FinCEN says a cybersecurity incident gave someone unauthorized access to some of its systems
summary: A notice on FinCEN's BSA E-Filing website says the agency is investigating a cybersecurity incident that 'resulted in unauthorized access to a limited subset of its systems'.
detail: FinCEN, the Treasury bureau that collects banks' suspicious activity reports, posted the notice on the evening of Tuesday Nov 24, according to The Record. A FinCEN official repeated it to Reuters on Nov 25. FinCEN has not said which systems were reached, when, or by whom.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: FinCEN's own notice, read on its website, states the unauthorized access in these words.
notes: Tier 1: read on bsaefiling.fincen.gov on Nov 25.

claim_text: FinCEN took some systems offline; the BSA E-Filing website still works but some services may not
summary: FinCEN says it took some systems offline as a precaution. Its notice says the BSA E-Filing website remains operational but some services may be temporarily unavailable. No restoration time has been given.
detail: The notice says FinCEN is 'working diligently to return all systems to normal operations as soon as possible'. It does not name the systems that are offline.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: FinCEN's notice says systems were taken offline and some services may be unavailable; Reuters quotes an official saying the same.
notes: Re-read the alert on every check: this is the service claim.

claim_text: FinCEN has moved filing deadlines to Dec 30 for filers hit by the disruption
summary: A FinCEN order dated Nov 24 gives certain filers with submissions due Nov 18 to Dec 29 until Dec 30, 2026 to file them, 'in response to a service disruption that is hindering filers' ability to adhere to reporting obligations'.
detail: The order (FIN-2026-R002) covers financial institutions that, as of Nov 18, used Secure Data Transfer Mode (SDTM) to file Bank Secrecy Act reports, and companies and individuals due to file a beneficial ownership report or update a FinCEN ID. Banks must still monitor for suspicious transactions, and can use FinCEN's hotline, which still works, to get urgent information to law enforcement. A FinCEN official told Reuters the agency had 'provided exceptive relief for filers that are not able to submit reports as a result of the disruption'. The order does not say when the disruption began or which systems are down.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: FinCEN's own order sets the Nov 18 to Dec 29 window and the Dec 30 deadline, and names who it covers; the alert and the official's statement to Reuters say deadlines are being extended.
notes: Tier 1: order PDF read on fincen.gov on Nov 25. FinCEN says it may modify or extend the order. Hotline number is on FinCEN's page; not repeated here.

claim_text: The FBI, CISA and outside forensic examiners are working with Treasury on the investigation
summary: A FinCEN official said Treasury is working with the FBI, the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) and third-party forensic examiners to work out the scope and impact.
detail: This comes from a FinCEN statement given to Reuters and to The Record. Neither the FBI nor CISA has said anything in public that we found.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: Two outlets quote FinCEN's statement; it is the agency's own word, so it is counted as one source.
notes: Upgrade if the FBI or CISA confirm their role.

claim_text: FinCEN says there is no evidence so far that its Bank Secrecy Act or beneficial ownership databases were breached
summary: FinCEN says that while forensic work goes on, there is no evidence of any breach of the Bank Secrecy Act or beneficial ownership databases.
detail: These databases hold the reports banks file on suspicious transactions and records of who owns companies. 'No evidence so far' is not the same as 'not breached': the investigation is not finished.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: Both outlets quote the agency's statement; it is FinCEN's word alone.

claim_text: Who got in, how and when is not known
summary: FinCEN has not said who got in, how, or when it began. No group has claimed responsibility, according to The Record.
detail: The Record notes that Chinese state-backed groups were accused of breaching the Treasury Department in 2024 and 2025, but nobody has linked those to this incident. Nothing we read names an attacker.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: None of the sources names an attacker, a method or a start date.

claim_text: Whether this is connected to breaches reported the same week at the CIA and other agencies
summary: The Record reports the FinCEN notice came the same day as reports that the CIA and other intelligence agencies had unclassified systems breached. No official has linked the two.
detail: Reuters also places the incident among a run of outages and disruptions at US systems this month. Neither outlet reports any evidence connecting them; the link is timing only.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: Both outlets mention other incidents for context, and neither reports a connection.
notes: Watch for an official statement linking or separating them.
